  2. Know-Why: Knowledge of principles, laws, and scientific theories explaining natural or social phenomena. Drives innovation and problem-solving by explaining underlying mechanisms.
  3. Know-How: Practical skills or expertise to perform tasks effectively. Key to operational efficiency and competitive advantage, as it is harder to replicate than explicit knowledge.
  4. Know-Who: Knowledge of social networks, including who possesses specific expertise or resources. Enhances collaboration and accelerates problem-solving by connecting knowledge sources.

PS: A structured classification of knowledge type in educational psychology

  1. Declarative Knowledge: Knowledge of facts, concepts, or information that can be explicitly stated or recalled (“knowing what”).
  2. Procedural Knowledge: Knowledge of how to perform tasks, procedures, or skills (“knowing how”).
  3. Conceptual Knowledge: Deep understanding of interconnected ideas, principles, or theories (“knowing why”).
  4. Metacognitive Knowledge: Awareness and regulation of one’s own thinking and learning processes (“knowing about knowing”).

Criticisms: Boundaries between categories (e.g., know-how vs. know-who) can blur in practice. Real-world problems often require blended knowledge types, which rigid classifications may overlook.

Framework Construction

Dual pathways of knowledge acquisition

Generally speaking, I tend to divide the ways of acquiring knowledge into two categories - structured and unstructured. Also, we can use other dualistic concepts, like institutionalized and practical. Institutionalized channels include formal education system (school/university), digital learning platform, etc. Practical channles cover professional experience, social observation, cross-scene experience, etc.

In my opinion, if the process of knowledge acquistion could cover ‘DIKW’, it is structured. Otherwisw, it is unstructured. There are 2 steps to achieve the goal of organizing the acquired knowledge.

For structured parts, we should clarify the knowledge framework;
For unstructured parts, we should transform data or “know-what” into knowledge “know-why”, with the details of “know-how”.

Propose the framework

Based on theoretical foundations and personal experience, I propose the framework of building knowledge systems. It is dual with five steps.

Unstructured

For the unstructured part, firstly, we should record experience objectively from a third perspective. Secondly, we should extract abstract concepts from records, such as pattern features and key variables. Thirdly, we should coupling the information moduels with academic theories. There are some tools could help the process. For example, the STAR-T method: Situation, Task, Action, Result, Thinking, Conceptualization.

Case:
Step 1. Record (STAR)
Situation: In Beijing, 2015, I joined in a startup project called ‘Chenxing Talent Plan’. This program aims to provide loans for college students and recover loans based on the percentage of students’ salaries after graduation.

Task: My job is to promote this project to target customers.

Action: There are two options for brand promotion - online and offline. I tried three methods to make offline campus promotions. The first is to communicate with the official to get supports, like establishing a enterprise-school organization, establishing a foundation, sponsorship for campus activities. Also, I tried online methods. I communicated with students’ union and organize an online speech through WeChat community.

Result: Obviously, the offline promotion failed in my school, because the enterprise did not provide sufficient resources. And the online speech succeeded. By the way, establishing a foundation and sponsorship for campus activities were successful in the other university, but I was just involved in and not primarily responsible for.

Step 2. Extraction (Thinking)
Why it failed? The enterprise should consider costs and benefits (short term and long term). For example, establishing a enterprise-school organization was a long term favourable plan, but it needed more funds in the short term. ‘Capital is short-sighted’, especially for the startup project.
Why it succeeded? In Beijing Jiaotong University, establishing a foundation and sponsorship for campus activities were successful, because the management had a relationship with the school. And the online speech was successful because of the low cost.

With limited resources in a startup project, we should choose low cost promotion channels at first. Appropriate content and KOL can be effective to attract the first batch of users. However, the content needs to be linked to the project.

Step 3. Conceptualization (MFUs)
Concepts: resources, costs, benefits, long term, shor term, channles, content, content carrier, customers/users, stakeholders, decision making
Relationships:

Step 4. Reconfiguration

Step 5. Creative Application

(See details in the next section)

Structured

For the structured part, in most cases, there are knowledge systems or knowledge maps while you are studying. For example, when you read articles, authors will list their hypotheses, methods, conclusions, etc. While you take courses or read books, teachers and authors will also introduce the outline, theories, practical methods, etc.

The problem is how you integrate this knowledge into your own system. Aiming to solve this problem, we should ‘split’ the information into smaller units. For instance, when we conduct literature review research, we will use framewroks to extract key information, such as TACI (Targets, Antecedents, Consequences, Interventions), SPIDER (Sample, Phenomenon of Interest, Design, Evaluation, Research type), etc.

In this part, I wanna introduce a word from the business research, MVP (Minimum Viable Product). MVP is the simplest version of a product that can be released to the market with just enough core features to satisfy early customers and validate a business idea. By analogy, when we process the structured knowledge, we should find the MFU, minimum feasible unit as the foundation of your knowledge system. When referencing MFU, we should understand it by common sense or MNK, minimum necessary knowledge, which should be easy to be measured or quantified.

Why should we use MFU? Let’s back to the case mentioned above. In terms of brand promotion, we divided it into online and offline. As for the online promotion, we chose online speech to attract customers. In this experience, online speech is the MFU. We can answer the question ‘How should we organize an online speech?’ through common sense. ‘Speech content, speaker, venue (WeChat) and audience (students).’

How about the courses, articles, books? We extract theories and ideas from them. For example, the ‘Easterlin Paradox’ states that at a point in time happiness varies directly with income, both among and within nations, but over time the long-term growth rates of happiness and income are not significantly related. In this case, MFUs are happiness and income.

As a matter of fact, in the academical field, we usually use CDI (Concept-Dimension-Index) to make research designs. But in different cases, MFUs could be concepts or indexes. The boundary is blur in practice. When we link different concepts (or MFUs) together, theories are formed. It could be linear or non-linear relationship, could be hierarchy, could be framework, could be workflow, etc. Now, I wanna propose steps to process structured knowledge.

Step 1. Outline
Outline the knowledge from authors’ perspectives.

Step 2. Distillation
Identify useful theories and ideas from the outline, including relationship between concepts, framework, models, etc.

Step 3. MFUs
Find MFUs of these theories and ideas, and make tags on them.

Step 4. Reconfiguration
Combine MFUs with distillation and extraction parts, to understand the relationship, hierarchy, framework, etc. Transform empirical knowledge and others’ knowledge into your own’s.

Step 5. Creative Application
Try to apply your knowledge in the real world!

entry.title: My_questions
entry.content:
My questions

In 2010, a brief talk with Xiaomin
(1) How does the society work?

In 2013, poetry study
(2) How poems attract readers? Imagery, rhythm, association.

In 2015, a sudden breakup
(3) How to handle troubled times and frustration?

In 2016, International business study:
(4) How goods are produced and sold globally?

In 2018. brand consulting
(5) How to build up a new brand? brand positioning
(6) How to spread a brand online and offline?
(7) How to evaluate the brand equity?
*** SUM: How can enterprises establish brand assets through brand communication?

In 2018~2019, business data analysis
(8) Which indexes the operation manager should focuses on? revenue, cost, profit, timeline, cooperation

In 2019, Kuaishou
(9) Which kind of content attracts users online? cover, icon, title, vertical content…
(10) How to build a SOP to promote efficiency?
(11) Invisible rights in the Big company? eg. frontline staff can decide the allocation of resources

In 2020~2021, UIC
(12) How innovation disseminates on Internet? S-curve
(13) What is the philosophy behind the brand theories? from product to brand, brand equity, brand relationship, brand engagement ……
(14) How can I combine complexity theories with brand or other social sciences?

In 2023~2025

(16) How information disseminates on Internet? SIR model
(17) How to apply machine learning models in social science research? SWB study
(18) Management information systems

entry.title: Delagation Theory
entry.content:
Baird, Aaron, and Likoebe M. Maruping. “The Next Generation of Research on IS Use: A Theoretical Framework of Delegation to and from Agentic IS Artifacts.” MIS Quarterly 45, no. 1 (March 1, 2021): 315–41. https://doi.org/10.25300/MISQ/2021/15882.

Presumption: the theoretical paradigm shift in the ==IS use== research - from “treating the IS artifact as a passive tool” to “agentic IS artifacts“.

Gap: The vast majority of IS use research, however, assumes that IS artifacts are tools that serve as a means to achieving a user’s ends.

Core:

  1. transferring rights and responsibilities for task execution and outcomes. [1]
  2. This new generation of agentic IS artifacts is imbued with the capacity to learn, adapt, act autonomously, and be aware of the need to act without being prompted by users. [2]

[^1]: 可以理解为“自组织”，“自进化”的观点。比如设计一套算法，在给予初始化的数据后，获得了一个结果。这个是传统的IS use所关注的，但是现在每天都有大量的数据投喂进这个算法，使得产出的结果出现了变化，而这里面，human responsibilities减少了，单纯的是Agentic IS artifacts在运作
[^2]: 许多基于人的责任在转移给新的agent，例如，汽车驾驶——>智能驾驶，这里面的agent从司机变成了program

entry.title: EWOM of Genshin Impact from a process perspective
entry.content:
EWOM of Genshin Impact: from a process perspective

1. Literature review

With the rapid development of Internet, electronic word-of-mouth (hereafter called eWOM) becomes more and more significant in the filed of marketing research. The extent literature have identified that eWOM plays an important role in the consumer behavior (eg., information adoption, consumer recommendations and consumer engagement). (Chu & Kim, 2011[1]) investigated determinants of consumer engagement in eWOM in SNSs, and identify tie strength, trust, normative and informational influence are positively associated with users’ overall eWOM behavior, whereas a negative relationship was found with regard to homophily. (Erkan & Evans, 2016 [2])developed a integrated model (named Information Acceptance Model) based on Information Adoption Model (IAM) and Theory of Reasoned Action (TRA) to confirm that quality, credibility, usefulness, adoption of information, needs of information and attitude towards information are key factors of eWOM in social media that influence consumers’ purchase intentions. (Yang, 2017[3]) explored three predictors to eWOM intentions: experience factor, knowledge sharing factors and technology acceptance factors. Furthermore, he also examined the moderating role of technology acceptance factors on the relationships between experience/knowledge sharing factors and eWOM intentions. From a perspective of product, (Park & Lee, 2009 [4]) discovered that the eWOM effect plays a greater role in experience goods than in search goods. (Lee & Shin, 2014 [5]) examined that review quality has different effects on the purchase intention for experienced goods and search goods. (Lin & Kalwani, 2018 [6]) built a conceptual model of eWOM signaling and screening to test the cross-cultural factors’ impact on the relationship between eWOM and product.

Besides, the platform is also a key factor in the research of eWOM. (Lee & Youn, 2009 [7]) found that when the review is positive, the eWOM platforms have the impact on consumer willingness to recommend the products to friends. (Tsao & Hsieh, 2015 [8]) designed an experiment to identify that the type of eWOM platforms moderate the influence of eWOM quality on eWOM credibility and purchase intention, especially in search goods. (Xu & Lee, 2020 [9]) found that linguistic characteristic, content of consumer reviews and managerial responses differ depending on platforms, by using a text mining approach to analyze data in the hotel industry. From the aspect of eWOM’s message, (Park & Kim, 2008 [10]) found that the effect of cognitive fit (the type of reviews) on purchase intention is stronger for experts than for novices while the effect of the number of reviews on purchase intention is stronger for novices than experts. (Teng & Khong, 2014 [11]) proposed that argument quality, source credibility, source attractiveness, source perception and source style are critical antecedents of persuasive eWOM messages. (Bao & Tang, 2014 [12]) demonstrated that eWOM of opinion leaders drives product sales due to their product experience and knowledge background.

As mentioned above, researchers have contributed a lot to the field of eWOM. However, most articles focused on the specific factors related to eWOM, such as product types, platforms, messages, adoption, impact, etc. Regrettably, they neglected that eWOM, as a type of communication, is a process. According to the definition given by Em Griffin, _‘Communication is the relational process of creating and interpreting messages that elicit a response [13] eWOM should also be a kind of relational process and researchers can fix more attention on this. And in this report, I will discuss the case ‘Genshin Impact (hereafter called Genshin)’ from a process perspective, and the analysis framework is mainly based on the research conducted by A. Rosario [14], who conceptualized three distinct stages in the eWOM process: eWOM creation, eWOM exposure and eWOM evaluation. As for the eWOM creation, consumers should be willing to create original and share existing content. The motivations of creation include altruism, social value from interaction, hedonic benefits, impression management and identity formation, balance restoration, venting, retribution, economic incentives. Also, opportunity to create based on instant internet access, low posting costs, variety of eWOM formats is important. And consumers should maintain the ability to create based on product knowledge, tech skill, proficiency, competencies. Referring to the eWOM exposure, there are some noticeable points. Consumers might actively seek exposure or accidentally be exposed to eWOM. Exposure depends on opportunities such as Internet access, platform characteristics or network effects. Generally speaking, consumers have motivations to actively seek exposure for reducing pre-purchase evaluation effort, perceived risks or just for the leisure. Finally, eWOM evaluation is also a concerned part. Usually, consumers’ motivation to evaluate eWOM are influenced by receivers, senders, message characteristics, opportunities determined by context and abilities of evaluations, like cognitive resources and prior knowledge.

2. Topic selection - Genshin Impact

In this report, I will choose Genshin as the study object. Genshin is a young brand in digital games, which was launched in Sept. 2020_._ As is known to all, Chinese digital game industry is a red ocean market. However, since 2020, relying on the huge success of Genshin, Mihoyo[15] (parent firm name) has become the TOP3 company in game industry. And the success of Genshin is closely related to the eWOM. For example, in the UGC platform Bilibili, there are more than 7 millions videos and over 60 billions view counts in the channel of Genshin.[16] Among such a large scale data, there are lots of players spontaneously create and upload videos related to Genshin, and these numerous videos will be exposed to the audiences, who might become the potential players. This is a typical eWOM process. Of course, similar phenomena are happening not only in domestic platforms (like Douyin, Kuaishou, Xigua, etc) but also in the foreign platforms (like FB, X, YouTube, etc). So, as a world-renowned brand, which is tightly related to eWOM, Genshin is a perfect study object. For a better understanding, I would like to draw the study boundary of this research. Genshin is a digital game, which is special compared with other ordinary goods. Game, as a ninth art in the world, in my opinion, is a kind of cultural product, which is highly connected to consumers’ experience. So, the product discussed in this study is ‘experience good’ and the analysis framework of eWOM communication is paid more attention on the ‘culture’.

Besides, the reason why I choose Genshin as my study object is also related to the sub-par performance of Genshin’s eWOM managerial policy. With these three years’ development, Genshin seems like used to ‘lying down policy’, which is a passive way to face the negative eWOM. They choose to not respond to the negative information and wait this kind of news fading way itself. For example, in April 2023, a Bilibili up ‘Chunshui’ posted a video to attack the Genshin’s pricing strategy, which is widely spreaded on the Internet. But Mihoyo did not do any response as usual. Except that, in the period of ‘Zhangcao’, which is a network word to describe that users have nothing to do in the game, Genshin’s operation team do not pay attention to the eWOM, and just wait for the next new game character to make topic propagation. In conclusion, Genshin focus on their game’s script shaping and character shaping, which is the key of their success, and also consumers are willing to actively propagandize Genshin themselves. But actually, as a mature brand, they should do more and better in terms of eWOM.

3. Discussion

3.1 Managerial guidelines

In this part, I will draw a eWOM communication outline for Genshin in details from a process perspective, which will be divided into three parts as mentioned in Section 1.

(1) EWOM creation

Benefit from the development of mobile Internet and social media platforms (eg., Douyin, Kuaishou, Bilibili, Xiaohongshu, etc) and the emergence of graphic and video editing tools (eg., Jianyin, Bijian, etc.), users have a fair chance to create eWOM contents without specialized knowledge. So, Genshin should focus on the construction of incentive mechanism to motivate users to create eWOM content. Firstly, Genshin should launch interesting topics for users. In terms of game content, it has done a really good work. But they can do other activities, like cooperation with museums and intangible cultural heritage, which can gather a good deal of support from both consumers and society. Users can realize social value from it and it’s also a kind of impression management for the potential users. Secondly, they can construct a good economic incentive mechanism to motivate users. For example, when users’ contents reach a set amount of view counts, likes or other indexes, they can be rewarded with gifts, cash or game tokens. Thirdly, Genshin should pay more attention to their own community, which provides users with a significant platform of identity formation.

(2) EWOM exposure

There are two parts of eWOM exposure. Firstly, Genshin should increase the eWOM communication which might be ‘accidentally’ exposed to new users. For example, the cooperation with different zones’ up-loaders to create eWOM content can effectively attract potential users. Secondly, aiming at users who actively seek for exposure, there are several situations, the main of which when users seek for exposure is that Genshin launches a new game character. And there will be two parties to make eWOM communication on Internet. One is taking care of character’s strength and the other is considering character’s traits, story lines. If Genshin wanna users focusing on the character itself, it should try to lead users, like supporting up-loaders’ re-creation around the character, which can also reduce pre-purchase evaluation for players. Also, users actively seek for exposure just for leisure. In this situation, Genshin has its advantages, because it maintains enough high-quality contents for users to re-create.

(3) EWOM evaluation

First of all, Genshin can motivate users to evaluate through incentive mechanism as mentioned above. Secondly, Genshin should increase opportunities for users to evaluate, like launching more kinds of activities, using more kinds of social platforms. Thirdly, Genshin should also educate users to know its emphasis on game content and give more supports for users who try to show the game maps, story lines, the mixed meanings of virtual world and the reality. Of course, they should construct a system to trace users evaluations.

(4) EWOM managerial Model
eWOM creation → eWOM exposure → eWOM evaluation
(image)

3.2 Managerial implications

This study suggested an model, which is down-to-earth for brands or companies to follow. Previous research focused on the relationship of eWOM factors, like product type as a moderator between eWOM and platforms, or a static analysis on the impacts, persuasion effects, antecedents of eWOM’s some specific attributes. This study provided a macroscopic guideline to the marketers and implicated that brands should not only focused on the specific data, like sales, exposures of their products, but also pay more attention on the whole process of eWOM communication.

3.3 Limitations

The model I suggested in this study is still a rough outline, and more attention is paid on the practical part. From an academical aspect, it lacks empirical support or a real down-to-earth project to identify the whole work flow. Besides, eWOM communication as a significant tool of marketing, it can be combined with the customer-based brand equity theory[17], which may provide more concrete measurement methods to monitor every stage of eWOM process. Also, in the eWOM creation part, Douglas Holt and Douglas Cameron’s theory can also be a good choice. In their opinion, cultural innovation is to deliver an innovative cultural expression, composed of ideology, myth and codes[18], which can provide marketers with an operable approach to deliver appropriate contents for consumers to share and recreate. So, in the future work, more theories can be combined together to make eWOM process better.

Reference

[1] Shu-Chuan Chu & Yoojung Kim (2011) Determinants of consumer engagement in electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM) in social networking sites. International Journal of Advertising. 30(1), 47-75.

[2] Erkan, I., & Evans, C. (2016). The influence of eWOM in social media on consumers’ purchase intentions: An extended approach to information adoption. Computers in Human Behavior, 61, 47-55.

[3] Yang, F. X. (2017). Effects of Restaurant Satisfaction and Knowledge Sharing Motivation on eWOM Intentions: The Moderating Role of Technology Acceptance Factors. Journal of Hospitality & Tourism Research, 41(1), 93–127.

[4] Park, C., & Lee, T. M. (2009). Information direction, website reputation and eWOM effect: A moderating role of product type. Journal of Business Research. 62(1), 61–67.

[5] Lee, EJ., Shin, S. Y. (2014). When do consumers buy online product reviews? Effects of review quality, product type, and reviewer’s photo. Computers in Human Behavior, 31, 356-366.

[6] Lin, H.-C., & Kalwani, M. U. (2018). Culturally Contingent Electronic Word-of-Mouth Signaling and Screening: A Comparative Study of Product Reviews in the United States and Japan. Journal of International Marketing, 26(2), 80–102.

[7] Lee, M., & Youn, S. (2009) Electronic word of mouth (eWOM): How eWOM platforms influence consumer product judgement. International Journal of Advertising. 28(3), 473-499.

[8] Tsao, WC., & Hsieh, MT. (2015) eWOM persuasiveness: do eWOM platforms and product type matter? Electronic Commerce Research. 15(4), 509-541.

[9] Xu, X., & Lee, C. (2020) Utilizing the platform economy effect through EWOM: Does the platform matter? International Journal of Production Economics, 227, 107663.

[10] Park, DH., & kim, S. (2008) The effects of consumer knowledge on message processing of electronic word-of-mouth via online consumer reviews. Electronic Commerce Research and Applications. 7(4), 399-410.

[11] Teng, S., Wei Khong, K., Wei Goh, W., & Yee Loong Chong, A. (2014). Examining the antecedents of persuasive eWOM messages in social media. Online Information Review. 38(6), 746-768.

[12] Bao, T., & Chang, S.T. (2014) Finding disseminators via electronic word of mouth message for effective marketing communications. Decision Support Systems. 67, 21-29.

[13] Em Griffin. (2012) A First Look at Communication Theory 8th. Publisher: McGraw-Hill.

[14] Babić Rosario, A., de Valck, K., & Sotgiu, F. (2019). Conceptualizing the electronic word-of-mouth process: What we know and need to know about eWOM creation, exposure, and evaluation. Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science, 48(3), 422–448.

[15] URL: https://www.mihoyo.com/

[16] URL: https://www.bilibili.com/v/channel/7945544/?tab=featured

[17] Keller, K. L. (1993). Conceptualizing, Measuring, and Managing Customer-Based Brand Equity. Journal of Marketing, 57(1), 1.

[18] Douglas Holt & Douglas Cameron. (2010) Cultural Strategy: Using Innovative Ideologies to Build Breakthrough Brands. Publisher: Oxford University Press.
